liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Scarlet Begonias** (2 reviews): The transition into Fire On The Mountain is called immaculate in the second set; A snappy transition into Fire On The Mountain sets the pace for the second set [9][16]
- **Satisfaction** (2 reviews): The performance of Satisfaction is described as pretty raucous by the listener; Listener believes the song just doesn't work for the band, wondering about Pig on vocals [17][19]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): A train wreck occurs during the song, though the high-energy show still kicks ass [17]
- **Friend Of The Devil** (1 review): Jerry plays the song really nice, contributing to a first set packed with goodies [16]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): The transition jam closing the first set is described as a monumental work of art [9]
- **Stella Blue** (1 review): The outro climax jam is perfectly executed with proper emphasis on every important note [15]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-12-09.sbd.motu.11626.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 25 songs; 184 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1981-12-09.sbd.miller.87349.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 24 songs; 184 min; rated 3.78/5 by 9 [2]. Said about its sound: Charlie Miller's soundboard recording sounds better than the poor live Event Center audio; Lead guitar sounds low, making vocals awkward and the instrument nearly inaudible; Recording is crisp with lots of separation and definition, cleaner than many official releases [11][12][13]
- **gd1981-12-09.158935.mtx.seamons.ht152.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 183 min [3]. Said about its sound: Light PA static is present throughout, though the matrix helps mask this issue; Above average waveform clipping occurred in the SBD source, particularly during this song [3]
- **gd1981-12-09.167567.nak300.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 25 songs; 180 min [4]
- **gd1981-12-09.senn421.wise.82199.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 25 songs; 180 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [6]. Said about its sound: Listener recalls this as the loudest and most raw Dead show they ever witnessed [10]

## Around the show

- Attendee walked to and from the CU Events Center, avoiding driving while high [10]
- Attendee attended despite finals stress and lack of money, living twenty miles away [11]
- Listener's original audience tape lacked the encore, so the sound differs from this recording [20]
- Show is slightly overshadowed by strong earlier performances that week but remains highly rated [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-12-09.sbd.motu.11626.shnf**: transferred by MOTU; source: SBD>Rm>Dat>CD [1]. Also: Zephyr patched Bird Song, Mama Tried, Mexicali Blues, Space, and The Other One; A reel splice occurred during the song, requiring a fade-in patch [1]
- **gd1981-12-09.sbd.miller.87349.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel (7 inch Reel @ 7.5ips 1/2trk) -> Dat -> CD [2]. Also: Jim Wise transferred Sennheiser 421 to master cassette then CD, cleaning flaws and fixing patches; The last eight seconds of Bird Song are supplied from the Sennheiser 421 source [2]
- **gd1981-12-09.158935.mtx.seamons.ht152.flac16**: source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro (FLAC > AIFF > Final Cut w/EQ > AIFF CD tracking via Audacity > FLAC16 via xACT w/meta-tagging) December 9, 2022 [3]. Also: AUD tape flips during He's Gone and The Other One were patched with Rip Tompkins' recording [3]
- **gd1981-12-09.167567.nak300.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 300 mics > Sony D5M (Maxell XLIIS 90) [4]. Also: Frank Streeter's Sennheiser 421 source supplies a thirteen-second patch in Drums [4]
- **gd1981-12-09.senn421.wise.82199.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Jim Wise; source: Sennheiser 421's > Sony TC-D5 > MAC > CD likely Nakamichi Dragon > HHB CDR burner > CDR [6]
